=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:246-259 (`_terminal_unchanged`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The newer block-label event check only considers events whose labels are still present (`carried = labels & set(unblock_ledger.BLOCK_LABELS)`, `event.get("label") in carried`).
  WHY: If another block label is applied after the close verdict and later removed while the original label remains, the stop still matches the old close verdict. The item is skipped as `terminal_unchanged` instead of being re-armed.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:376-388 (`select`; poller marks `history_incomplete` at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 19433-19439 and 19460) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `terminal_unchanged` is returned before `history_incomplete` is checked.
  WHY: The poller fetches only the last 30 comments, so a newer non-bot comment can fall outside the window and leave `_has_new_evidence` with nothing to re-arm on. The branch skips the item before the existing full-history verification can run.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:264-273 (`_last_run_times`; projection at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh lines 19464-19465) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_last_run_times` excludes runs by checking `status` for `cancelled` or `skipped`, but the poller projects `status` without `conclusion`.
  WHY: GitHub reports those runs as `status: completed`, so a recently cancelled or skipped judge run counts as the latest run and can suppress an escalated fix-up recheck for 24 hours.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/unblock_scan.py (`_terminal_unchanged`, the `carried` computation and label-event filter) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The re-arm check only considers block-label events whose labels are still on the issue (`carried = labels & set(unblock_ledger.BLOCK_LABELS)`, `if event.get("label") in carried`).
  WHY: In the worked scenario `ai:validation-failed` is applied at T=3 and removed at T=4, while `ai:blocked` remains. `carried` is only `{"ai:blocked"}`, `episode` stays at T=0, and the item is skipped as `terminal_unchanged` although a material new block-label event occurred.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py (`_last_run_times`, filter `run.get("status") in ("cancelled", "skipped")`) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The filter checks `status`, but GitHub reports a cancelled run as `status: completed` with `conclusion: cancelled`, and the poller projection (scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19465) has no `conclusion`.
  WHY: A cancelled or startup-failed judge run still sets `last_runs[N]` and starts the 24-hour `fixup_escalated` skip. The delay is up to a day, small and self-correcting.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:246-258 (`_terminal_unchanged`; `carried = labels & set(unblock_ledger.BLOCK_LABELS)`, event filter at line 257) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The re-arm check only counts block-label events for labels the item still carries. `_has_new_evidence` (lines 216-231) looks at comments only, so the module docstring condition ("since the marker there is no new block label event", line 53) is not implemented.
  WHY: Example: the item carries `ai:blocked`, a close verdict lands for stop `blocked` at T, and `ai:scope-blocked` is applied at T+2h then removed by label repair. The labeled event is filtered out by `in carried`, so the item is skipped every tick and the judge never re-runs. Suggested fix: count events for any label in `unblock_ledger.BLOCK_LABELS`.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:264-274 (`_last_run_times`, filter at line 268; projection at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19465) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The filter never matches, since `conclusion` is not projected and cancelled/skipped are conclusions, not statuses. The same predicate pre-exists in `_busy_items` (line 286).
  WHY: A judge run cancelled by concurrency or failing at startup still starts the 24-hour `fixup_escalated` window, contradicting the function's own docstring (line 265). Suggested fix: project `conclusion` in the poller's jq and filter on it.
- scripts/unblock_scan.py:376-380 (precedes the `history_incomplete` gate at lines 385-388) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The terminal skip is decided before the incomplete-history guard, so a `terminal_unchanged` item never reaches the `verify_history` path.
  WHY: The window is the newest 30 comments with `updatedAt` mapped into `created_at` (line 19455). The residual miss is an older trusted comment outside the window, edited after the close, which leaves the item reported as `terminal_unchanged`. Suggested fix: return `False` from `_terminal_unchanged` when `info.get("history_incomplete")` is set.
- HARDENING: none; the `[bot]` ordering and non-dict `info` candidates were checked and dropped. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
